headline: Learned models integrate spatial and single-cell omics across modalities and tissues
label: Spatial Single Cell Computational Methods
summary: Spatial and single-cell profiling now spans morphology, multiomic, and perturbation data, demanding scalable and robust inference methods.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned or statistical modeling that extracts spatial, mechanistic, and cross-modal information from single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. Several preprints address spatial context directly: STITCH/KSTITCH links size-independent cell contour shape to gene expression in situ, SPARQ-MI performs end-to-end spatial phenotyping of multiplexed melanoma imaging, and STAMO applies graph attention to diagonally integrate unpaired spatial multi-omics slices. Integration robustness is another focus, with one study showing that embedding-based batch correction can distort gene-gene correlations. Generative and foundation models, including HoloCell and GeroEngine, extend this paradigm to large-scale profiles and aging trajectories. What is new is the emphasis on validating inference itself, including annotation evaluation without ground truth (ISC) and structured imputation diagnostics for sparse space biology data.
